messages:
Alice SRE: flagged by support — customer reports p99 spike for /v1/generate to ~1200ms starting ~04:20 UTC. dropping into thread for triage.
Carla (Support): customer acme-co reported retries + intermittent 504s. Started right after a deploy at ~04:15. They attached a sampling of request IDs.
Ben (Oncall): thanks — taking lead. Is it single-region or global?
Dave Infra: looks isolated to eu-west-1. Other regions (us-east-1, ap-south-1) look normal. There was a canary push at 04:13 that included a quantization kernel update.
Alice SRE: grabbing traces now. Early signal: KV cache hit rate for route /v1/generate dropped from ~94% to ~60% around 04:14. Latency spike aligns with cache thrash & increased GC on several pods.
Ben (Oncall): possible theory: new model rollout changed tokenization or initial prefixes and invalidated warm cache leading to heavy decode cost. Mitigations to try: 1) enable route-level fallback to previous compatible model, 2) increase rate-limit headroom/circuit-breaker thresholds temporarily to avoid noisy throttling.
Carla (Support): I'll inform customer we are triaging and may flip them to fallback briefly. They prefer a quick fix over waiting for full rollback.
Dave Infra: I can cut canary back to 0% now (rollback canary). Doing that first while Alice prepares fallback.
deploy-bot: deploy canary percent set to 0 by dave at 04:28 UTC.
Alice SRE: applied route fallback to redwood-quant-stable for the affected route at 04:29 UTC. Monitoring...
Ben (Oncall): visible improvement: p99 dropped from 1200ms -> ~180ms within 1m after fallback + rollback. No more 504s. Marking immediate impact mitigated.
Carla (Support): customer confirmed latency restored and no errors now. They appreciate the quick response. :tada:
Alice SRE: follow-ups / action items: 1) add automatic cache warming/migration step to model rollout pipeline (warm prefixes to avoid cold-KV storm), 2) add SLO guardrail rule: if p99 > 2x baseline for >5m post-deploy, auto-trigger fallback + page oncall, 3) tune circuit-breaker to avoid cascading throttles during model swap.
Ben (Oncall): creating follow-up ticket and assigning owners: @Alice SRE (postmortem + warm cache), @Dave Infra (deploy pipeline rollback safety), @Carla (customer comms).
Alice SRE: quick playbook snippets to add to runbook:
```
# force route fallback (admin)
POST /admin/routes/fallback
Content-Type: application/json
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "model": "redwood-quant-stable", "ttl_seconds": 600 }

# rollback canary (ops)
POST /ops/deployments/canary
{ "service": "runtime", "percent": 0 }

# temporarily increase rate-limit headroom for route
PATCH /admin/routes/ratelimit
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "burst": 200, "rate": 1000 }
```
Ben (Oncall): notes for playbook: include exact metrics to watch (p95/p99, cache hit ratio, GC pause %), thresholds, and the commands above. Also add a preflight check in rollout CI: simulate cache-warm at smaller scale.
Carla (Support): marking case resolved on our side and sending post-incident note to customer with summary + ETA for improvements.
Alice SRE: assigning postmortem to @Alice SRE and @Dave Infra; support owner @Carla. We'll post a short incident summary to #incidents and link this thread. Closing operational thread.
